Title: Atmospheric degradation of 4-hydroxy 4-methyl 2-pentanone with OH in the gas phase at 297 K
Authors: Chantal Sleiman, Gisèle El Dib, Antoine Tabet, André Canosa
Description: The reaction of 4-hydroxy-4-methyl-2-pentanone (4H4M2P) with OH radicals was investigated in the gas-phase using an absolute rate method at room temperature and over the pressure range of 10 to 745 Torr in He and air as diluent gases. The rate coefficients were measured with the Pulsed Laser Photolysis method (PLP) to produce OH and the Laser Induced Fluorescence technique (LIF) to detect the fluorescence of OH radicals. An average value of (4.5±1.5)×10-12 cm3molecule-1s-1 was obtained. This study is the first absolute determination of the rate coefficient of 4H4M2P with OH at room temperature as a function of pressure and the nature of diluent gases. No pressure dependence of the rate coefficient was observed. The obtained results are compared with those of other hydroxyketones in terms of the structure reactivity relationship. Authors: Ch El-Gemayel, F Jumel, N Abouchi, J Constantin, A Tabet, D Zaouk
Description: There is a need for consistent approach to interpret and to optimize the testing of clinical medical equipment. We propose a model for global simulating of biomedical equipments (including human interaction models). This paper begins by an in-silico study for type 1 diabetes mellitus patients using a mathematical model, implementation of a simple control algorithm, than generating virtual patients in order to have multiple scenarios to analyze performance. Finally, we associate it with a control-variability grid analysis in order to do a step to construct a clinical trial simulator.

Title: A new framework for analyzing the performance of the glucose-insulin system
Authors: CH El-Gemayel, F Jumel, N Abouchi, J Constantin, A Tabet, D Zaouk
Description: The ability to develop a testing model for analyzing the performance of any embedded biomedical devices can be very useful in medical research. This paper begins by the glucose insulin system and creates a new framework in order to test the performance of all system components. The framework consists of simulating a mathematical model of human body in order to implement in a microcontroller, developing a control algorithm for the model and applying parametric models of activities to show how medical devices can be interconnected to form a physiological closed-loop system. Finally a new tester model with the ability to satisfy medical decision criteria has been created. Simulation results show the performance of the tester to validate glucose insulin system in order to avoid risk taking on patients.

Title: The effect of the air velocity on the collection efficiency of microorganisms by impaction method
Authors: Antoine Tabet, Ch El-Gemayel, A Msaed, MN Sabra, G El Dib
Description: The effect of the air velocity on the collection efficiency of microorganisms was examined in this work. The study was carried out using a bio impactor developed and validated in our laboratory. Six sampling sites were chosen to perform measurements at different air velocities (5m/s, 10m/s and 20m/s). Before measurements, the air velocity was calculated and modified by varying the aspiration flow and the nozzle diameter of the used device. The air velocity of 20m/s was found to yield the maximum of collection efficiency. The experiments and results are described and discussed in the paper.

Title: Development of a bio-impactor with an adjustable collection distance, effect of Dfs on the CE
Authors: A Tabet, Ch El-Gemayel, L El-Khoury, MN Sabra, G El Dib
Description: In this study, a new modern bio-impactor with adjustable parameters was designed and constructed. A series of sampling were performed to validate our new device. The bacteria level in the indoor air of several sites was measured in this work by using simultaneously our new device and a commercial one. These measurements showed that the collection efficiency provided by our device is better than that of the commercial bio-impactor. The effect of the collection distance on the collection efficiency was studied as well.

Title: Microbial Air Samplers
Authors: Antoine Tabet, Gisèle El Dib, Antonio Khoury
Description:
The subject of inhaled bacteria is among the famous topic of current research. A precise bio-impactor with high resolution and fast response time is a must to measure and identify these airborne bacteria.
It is to be noted that Stewart studied in 1995 the shock and the stress effect on the aspired microbes at the velocity from 24 to 250 m/s. The highest recovered rate of viable cells obtained at a speed of 40 m/s for Pseudomonas, whereas the aspiration speed of Micrococcus was around 24m/s. This study shows the impact of aspiration speed parameter on the collection process.
